security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, protein terminology, or PyTorch API names. Confirmed risks are limited to intended Forge network use, local cache or checkpoint writes, and unsafe pickle loading in copied examples.

remediation.issue: Unsafe pickle deserialization appears in cache and checkpoint examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pickle with safer formats where possible, or document that cache files must come only from trusted local workflows.

remediation.issue: Forge examples use external endpoints and API tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to store tokens in environment secrets and warn before sending sensitive sequences to Forge.

remediation.issue: Cache and output examples write files in the working directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use explicit output directories, check before overwriting files, and document what data is stored locally.

content.value_statement: Protein design workflows can be hard to plan across sequence, structure, function, and embeddings. This skill provides practical ESM3, ESM C, and Forge API guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains local ESM3 setup for protein sequence generation.
Shows Forge API usage for remote ESM3 inference.
Guides structure prediction and inverse folding workflows.
Describes ESM C embedding extraction for downstream analysis.
Provides workflow examples for GFP design, variants, clustering, and function prediction.
limitations: It does not validate generated proteins experimentally.
Forge workflows require external API access and may send protein data to a cloud service.
Large models need significant GPU resources or paid hosted inference.
Examples are documentation snippets and may need adaptation for current ESM SDK versions.

use_cases.title: Plan Generative Protein Designs
use_cases.description: Use ESM3 guidance to create masked sequence prompts, generate candidates, and plan validation steps.

use_cases.title: Build Embedding Pipelines
use_cases.description: Use ESM C examples to extract representations for classification, clustering, or similarity tasks.

use_cases.title: Run Scalable Forge Jobs
use_cases.description: Use Forge API patterns for batch inference, retries, rate limits, and caching.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Model Choice
prompt_templates.prompt: I am new to ESM. Compare ESM3 and ESM C for my protein task and recommend a model path.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Sequence Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an ESM3 workflow for this target function, sequence length, constraints, and validation plan: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Create Embedding Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an ESM C embedding pipeline for these sequences, including batching, caching, clustering, and evaluation outputs: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Design Forge Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Forge API batch inference plan with retry strategy, rate limits, token handling, and privacy controls for: [project].

output_examples.input: I need candidate sequences for a fluorescent protein family.
output: Recommended ESM3 model choice with rationale.
Prompting strategy for masked sequence and function conditioning.
Validation checklist for structure, function, and biosafety review.

output_examples.input: I have 5,000 protein sequences for clustering.
output: ESM C embedding workflow with batching guidance.
Similarity and clustering plan for representative selection.
Storage guidance for outputs and trusted cache files.

output_examples.input: I want to use Forge for production inference.
output: Forge model selection guidance for cost and quality.
Retry and rate-limit strategy for batch jobs.
Token handling and data privacy checklist.

best_practices: Keep Forge API tokens in environment secrets and never place real tokens in prompts or files.
Start with smaller models and limited batches before scaling expensive inference.
Validate generated designs with independent structure, function, and biosafety review steps.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated proteins as experimentally validated results.
Do not send proprietary or sensitive sequences to cloud inference without approval.
Do not load pickle cache files from untrusted locations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan ESM3, ESM C, and Forge API workflows for protein modeling and analysis.

faq.question: Can it run ESM models by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You need the ESM SDK, model access, and suitable compute.

faq.question: Does Forge require an API token?
faq.answer: Yes. Forge examples require a token from EvolutionaryScale and send requests to an external service.

faq.question: Is it suitable for local-only work?
faq.answer: Yes, for supported open-weight models. Larger Forge-only models require remote access.

faq.question: Does it guarantee protein function?
faq.answer: No. Generated sequences require independent computational, experimental, and biosafety validation.

faq.question: What should I protect when using it?
faq.answer: Protect API tokens, proprietary sequences, generated structures, cache files, and experimental plans.
